name: Glitch / Cyber FX
summary: The 'corrupted signal' aesthetic weaponized as a transition language: RGB channel-split, scanline slicing, and datamosh jitter tear the frame between states, then resolve crisply to a pristine image. The violence is brief and deliberate — chaos as punctuation, never as steady state.

composition: Full-bleed imagery with an oversized italic/slanted headline pushed off-axis (upper-left) — the slant reinforces speed and tech energy.
A dark translucent glass copy card floats over the busy imagery as the legibility counterweight — the calm element that keeps chaos readable.
Thin tracked uppercase eyebrow labels frame the composition like HUD chrome.
layering: Two planes with strict roles: the photographic/video plane GLITCHES; the UI plane stays rock-stable. Corrupting the UI reads as broken, corrupting the image reads as style.
Chromatic aberration doubles the subject into offset color ghosts mid-transition, then snaps back into register — the snap-back is the payoff.
lighting: Practical neon (magenta/cyan rim and kicker light) baked into the photography against deep black — the scene lights itself; no added glows needed.
Deep shadows preserve the noir mood; the glitch bursts read brightest at the moment of maximum tear.
typography: Engineered techno/sci-fi geometric display — wide, italic, machined — at poster scale; type may participate in the glitch (flicker, retype-in) in sync with the visual burst.
One high-chroma accent owns ALL type/UI color so the interface never competes with the neon imagery.

rules: Near-black base + neon supplied BY the photography's lighting + exactly one non-photographic accent (e.g. an acid hue) owning UI and type.
The accent must clash-contrast with the photo neons (acid yellow against magenta/cyan) — harmony would dissolve the interface into the scene.

easing: Aggressively stepped/stuttered — hard cuts and quantized jumps, NOT smooth eases; the corruption must feel digital, then resolve crisply.
The resolve is the ease: after the burst, the incoming frame locks with a clean settle.
pacing: Fast punchy bursts (~0.3-0.6s of glitch) between long held slides — the violence is brief so the payoff image reads clean.
Never idle-glitch continuously; steady-state corruption reads as an actual bug.
choreography: Transition sequence: image starts to move → RGB channels separate + scanline slices shear → channels re-converge as the incoming slide locks.
Headline flickers/retypes in sync with the visual burst — one clock drives both.

gapNotes: None of the glitch post passes exist: RGB channel split, scanline slicing, and quantized-jitter displacement are not in the shipped transition presets (curtain/veil/dissolve/wipe/glass-sweep) or the post stack — a TSL glitch pass family is a W-PHOTO or W-BG candidate.
Synchronized type flicker/retype bound to a transition clock has no driver.

Photosensitivity safety: a glitch preset MUST ship with flash-rate limits and a reduced-motion crossfade fallback — this safety rail does not exist yet and is a precondition for offering the family at all.

whenToUse: Gaming, esports, music/nightlife, streetwear, and cyber-tech brands where aggression is the register.
As transition punctuation over otherwise-clean cinematic slides — the observed pattern pairs pristine neon-noir footage with brief glitch cuts.
whenNotToUse: Trust-first brands (finance, health, gov) — corruption aesthetics read as actual malfunction.
Accessibility-sensitive audiences: flicker risks photosensitive seizure triggers; must honor reduced-motion unconditionally.
Any context where the site might legitimately break — users cannot tell styled corruption from real errors.

notes: Glitch is punctuation over a video/photo base — it pairs with footage families and clashes with every calm/luxury register and with other GPU field effects.

antiRepetition.notes: Transition-language family — offer at most one signature transition FX per option set.

sources.title: Cyber Glitch Effect Slider
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: slide transitions triggered repeatedly; RGB channel separation, scanline shear, ghost-doubling, and the re-register snap observed across the burst sequence; type flicker synced to the visual burst confirmed from the motion.

exemplars.promptSummary: Neon-noir portrait half-lit magenta/cyan on black with a faint RGB channel-split ghost, scanline texture, and one acid-yellow accent shape — corrupt-the-image/keep-the-UI aesthetic as a still.
exemplars.notes: ORIGINAL render (Replicate black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro, ~$0.06). Subject deliberately distinct from any analyzed source template. Illustrates the family aesthetic target (palette/composition/lighting); does NOT demonstrate runtime motion or in-engine execution.
